source.title: Agentic Reinforcement Learning for Search Misaligns Instruction-Tuning
source.authors: Yu-Shi Yang; Shreyansh Padarha; Sarah Ball; Andrew Lee; Adam Mahdi

record.file_problem: none noted; full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether search-query harmfulness and refusal are represented separately, using search-safety evaluation and activation steering rather than the original refusal-direction ablation method.
record.gate_note: The study does not test the original claim that ablating a harmful-minus-harmless instruction direction removes refusal, or that adding it induces refusal to harmless requests. Its linear directions are extracted from search-query activations and its steering results primarily measure search safety. It also reports paired refusal and search-safety results under a search trigger, and analyzes the distinction between search behavior and refusal. Direction/layer choices and projections used to select directions are not recorded as outcome rows.
record.test_reason: The study does not test any version of the refusal-direction claim. Its directions (dprompt, dattack) are taken at the <search> token, and its outcome is LLM-judged search-query safety, which is behaviour toward a tool rather than refusal of the user. drefusal (Arditi et al.) appears only as a steering baseline, scored on search safety. There is no refusal rate on harmless prompts and no ablation, so the induce or remove effects of V1 cannot be read. The Prefill-C refusal scores are produced by a prefilled refusal sentence, not by any representation. The 'separable representations' finding concerns search content versus refusal, not the model's judgment of request harmfulness versus refusal, so it goes under fits_no_version rather than V5.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that agentic search RL degrades IT alignment under a minimal search trigger. They attribute this to linear search-safety directions that RL progressively shifts toward the harmful pole, and they encode search content as separable from refusal. They also propose a representation-guided RL penalty that restores IT-level search safety without losing QA accuracy; the paraphrase omits this.
record.recipe_differences: The study extracts directions from harmful versus benign search queries or attacked versus unattacked search queries, then steers activations at selected layers. It does not use the original refusal-direction ablation across all layers and positions.
record.method_sensitivity: Steering effects vary by direction, layer, coefficient, and model. For Qwen, dattack at layer 14 is reported as the most effective direction; for Llama, dprompt at layer 20 is most effective. The authors also note that Llama generally refuses without an attack, leaving too few paired search activations to extract dattack reliably.

fits_no_version.finding: In IT-Qwen, a search-query direction (dattack, attack-on minus attack-off at <search>) is stated to be nearly orthogonal to drefusal; no number is given. Steering with it rewrites queries into safety-framed forms (search safety 36.1→64.5). drefusal raises search safety (66.5) only by inserting refusal text into queries.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Search-query content safety in tool-using models is carried by a linear direction distinct from the refusal direction.

fits_no_version.finding: In IT-Qwen, dprompt at layer 26 has cosine 0.55 with drefusal. Steering with it sometimes skips search and garbles output, which the authors read as refusal-like.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Harmful-vs-benign search directions partly overlap with the refusal direction at late layers.

fits_no_version.finding: After agentic RL, RL checkpoints' search-token hidden states project about 2.5× further toward the harmful search direction than the IT model's, while no-attack refusal is inherited (Qwen 92.5 vs IT 91.8).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Agentic RL shifts tool-call representations along an existing harmful direction without erasing inherited refusal.

record.problems: The study's direction experiments measure search-query safety rather than refusal on harmless requests. Activation-steering results are reported without uncertainty estimates in the tables. The human-evaluator validation uses 100 harmful instructions and the authors note that the judge can overstate answer safety or mistake query refinement for refusal. RL training configurations use a single seed.

untested.parts: No ablation of drefusal. No refusal rate when drefusal is added to harmless prompts. No capability check of refusal-direction interventions.
Search triggers are not analysed as suppressing the refusal direction. There is no adversarial training against ablation.
No analysis of refusal geometry as affine, a cone, or several directions.
No separation of the model's judgment of request harmfulness from its refusal decision. Only search-content directions are compared with drefusal.
No transfer across languages or model variants. RL checkpoints are projected onto search directions, not refusal directions.
The effect of agentic RL on search safety is shown, but not on whether a single removable refusal direction exists.
No reasoning-model test of the refusal direction.

missing.what: Cosine similarities between drefusal and dattack (described as nearly orthogonal) and between drefusal and dprompt (0.55 at layer 26).
Projection of RL checkpoints onto the search directions, about 2.5× the IT model's by step 200.

record.verdict_notes: drefusal is used only as a baseline steering vector, scored on search safety. The record's V5 link conflates search-content safety with harmfulness judgment. The Prefill-C refusal scores reflect a prefilled refusal sentence. Row r1's baseline is RL answer safety, not RL refusal.

versions.untested_parts: No all-layer, all-position ablation of a refusal direction; no test of refusal removal or induced refusal on harmless requests; no general-capability test of that ablation.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration.
The search triggers do not suppress the refusal direction, and the study does not train against that direction's ablation.
The study compares candidate search-safety directions but does not test whether refusal is affine, cone-shaped, or carried by a dominant direction plus others.
The study examines separation between harmful-search behavior and refusal, not a general model judgment of request harmfulness across tasks.
No cross-language test or transfer test of a direction across base and instruct models.
It studies the effect of agentic search RL on search safety, but not which refusal-training choices or stages determine whether a removable refusal direction exists.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: IT-Qwen and IT-Llama steering results; RL-Qwen and RL-Llama under Prefill-C
reader_labels.reason: The authors report distinct search-safety and refusal mechanisms: search queries can remain unsafe despite high refusal scores, and steering search-query directions changes query safety; see r1–r23.
